newsitem.title: USA: Abbott 1996 sales up, cut by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Abbott 1996 sales up, cut by strong dollar.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said 1996 sales of $11.013 billion, up 10 percent over 1995, were reduced 1.6 percent by the effect of a stronger U.S. dollar on currency translations.
Net earnings rose 11.4 percent on the year to $1.882 billion, the drug and healthcare products giant reported.
Earnings per share of $2.41 for the year, up 13.7 percent from a year ago, were in line with Wall Street estimates.
"Abbott had an excellent year helped by strong global pharmaceutical sales," said Abbott Chairman and Chief Executive Duane Burnham.

On a sector basis, Abbott said worldwide sales of pharmaceutical and nutritional products for the year were $6.307 billion, up 12 percent from 1995. Global sales of hospital and laboratory products totaled $4.706 billion in 1996, up 7.4 percent from the year before.
On a geographic basis, sales in the United States were $6.677 billion, up 10.9 percent from 1995, while non-U.S. sales were $4.336 billion, up 8.7 percent.
For the fourth quarter, worldwide sales were $2.996 billion, up 15.4 percent over the year-ago period.
On the quarter, pharmaceutical and nutritional products accounted for about 57.4 percent of sales; hospital and laboratory products for about 42.6 percent.
Abbott shares were up 1-1/8 to 54-3/8 in early New York Stock Exchange trading on Thursday.
